claims.claim: Our fiscal regime label tells you where stocks go next
claims.rule: S&P 500 returns 5 to 60 sessions after Supportive or Restrictive spells differ from the base rate, after multiple-testing correction
claims.evidence: No test survived the multiple-testing correction (0 of 26). The label describes the fiscal state; it does not forecast the market.

claims.rule: 4-week changes in Fed balance sheet minus Treasury account minus reverse repo move with the S&P 500 over the same 4 weeks
claims.evidence: Correlation -0.06 (permutation p=0.30). The familiar chart reflects both series trending up, not moving together.

claims.rule: The 4-week change predicts the S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days
claims.evidence: Pre-registered result: the correlation test passed, the trading-rule test did not. Correlation +0.13 (p=0.029), under 2% of the variance; trading on its sign: +0.8 points per period, 95% CI [-0.1, +1.9], not significant. The small lead comes from the Fed balance sheet; the Treasury account and reverse repo parts show none.

claims.claim: Weak auctions push yields up on the day
claims.rule: Lower bid-to-cover than the previous 6 auctions goes with a larger rise in yield from the prior close to the auction-day close
claims.evidence: Correlation -0.15 (p=0.0003); weakest tenth of auctions +1.2bp on the day against +0.1bp for the rest.

claims.claim: Weak auctions keep pushing yields up
claims.rule: The same demand surprise predicts the yield change over the next 5 trading days
claims.evidence: Correlation +0.03 (p=0.47); after the weakest tenth, yields moved -1.1bp over the next week against -0.3bp. Priced within the day.

claims.claim: Record margin debt signals a market top
claims.rule: S&P 500 returns over the 12 months after FINRA margin debt sets a record are lower than after other months
claims.evidence: After records: +6.4% next 12 months against +7.5% otherwise (difference 95% CI [-9.1, +4.5] points). A 20% fall followed 4% of records against 20% of other months.

claims.claim: A surge in margin debt signals a market top
claims.rule: Same test when year-on-year margin debt growth is in the top tenth of its history
claims.evidence: After surges: -4.4% against +9.6% (95% CI [-25.7, +7.0] points). Lower on average, but too few episodes to separate from chance.

claims.claim: An inverted yield curve means a recession is coming
claims.rule: An NBER recession starts within 24 months of the 10-year minus 3-month spread turning negative
claims.evidence: 4 of 5 inversions were followed by a recession and 4 of 4 recessions were preceded by one. False alarm: 2022-11. One hit, 2020, was the pandemic. A record, not a significance test.

claims.claim: Withheld taxes give an early read on wage growth
claims.rule: Daily Treasury withheld taxes improve on last month's BEA wage figure for the month BEA has not yet published
claims.evidence: Average miss 0.61 points against 0.59 for last month's BEA figure (gain 95% CI [-0.09, +0.02]); direction right 85 of 154 months.
